newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland cuts sugar export subsidies to one percent.
newsitem.headline: Poland cuts sugar export subsidies to one percent.

text.p: Poland set the amount of subsidies for sugar exports from October 1, 1996 to September 30, 1997 at one percent of the price of the sugar sold domestically, the government said in a statement on Monday.
Previously the subsidy was two percent of the price of domestic sugar sales.

The government said the subsidy could not be larger than the difference between the minimum price of sugar, which had previously been set at 1,200 zlotys per tonne, and the price of sugar on the London Commodities Exchange in the week before the deal.
The amount of subsidised sugar between October 1, 1996 and January 1, 1997 will be 122,900 tonnes, in line with World Trade Organisation agreements.
From January 1, 1997 to September 30, 1997 it will be 118,300 tonnes.
